title: How do you guys actually USE AI in gamedev?
author: More-Drink2211
selftext:
For context, I just made a bunch of three.js games using Gemini, just for a start. Now looking at videos where they are merging Minecraft and GTA into one, it doesn't seem like you can just ask ChatGPT, "Hey, please make me a video game about building but its GTA"

So as the question implies, do you guys:  
\- Use AI to generate concept art and ideas and then make the models and game yourself?  
\- Use AI to make the game itself, like physically making the models, assets and code in actual game engines like UE5 and Unity? If so, how, considering I can't get Gemini to make a single line of HTML without messing up something?  
\- Something in between?

I would like to learn more about this, I'm not exactly an AI genius, so forgive me if this post sounds poorly worded or has incorrect terminology.

comments.author: zayelion
comments.body: I use given when then,  to right short requirements.

comments.author: RoyInProgress
comments.body:
Hey!

Short answers:  
“(do you) Use AI to generate concept art and ideas and then make the models and game yourself?”

I have the ideas and make the decisions, AI makes the art, sprites, the game and how it comes together.

“(do you) - Use AI to make the game itself, like physically making the models, assets and code in actual game engines like UE5 and Unity? If so, how, considering I can't get Gemini to make a single line of HTML without messing up something?” 

Yes, Claude / Codex does everything. I never write or review a single line of code. How? The frontier models are really good. Using the right infrastructure, clear requirements and good prompts - you can come a long way.

This is my game currently:

comments.author: sevenoutdb
comments.body: All of the above I guess. I do chat with Claude Code about specific features, and I think that providing the additional context really makes the difference between a workable result and an excellent result. I’m making yet another 2D space game but it’s really starting to feel special and interesting. Claude Code and Codex are not what I use for concept art, I still use Midjourney for this purpose, and I hand draw or trace from concept art into vector graphics. This makes the art feel much more imperfect and human.
